html:
The Mothers of the Plaza de Mayo are a movement of Argentine women whose children were disappeared by the military dictatorship. They first gathered in the Plaza de Mayo in Buenos Aires on 30 April 1977.

When they could get no answers about their missing children in the Dirty War, fourteen mothers met in front of the presidential palace. Because the police banned standing groups, they walked in pairs around the square. They wore white headscarves, first made from babies' nappies, embroidered with their children's names. Some of their founders, including Azucena Villaflor, were themselves disappeared in 1977.

They kept marching every Thursday for decades. The Grandmothers of the Plaza de Mayo have used DNA tests to find over a hundred stolen grandchildren. The Mothers became a world symbol of peaceful resistance and the search for justice in Argentina, like those who opened the Archives of Terror in Paraguay.
sum: The Mothers of the Plaza de Mayo are a movement of Argentine women whose children were disappeared by the military dictatorship. They first gathered in the Plaza de Mayo in Buenos Aires on 30 April 1977.
